A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeMixer++ work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-K are readable and support reliable matching across deletions, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original TimeMixer++ benchmark results across eight tasks, component ablations, representation analyses, efficiency measurements, and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains original TimeMixer++ experimental results and analyses in Section 4 and the appendices, including revised numerical uncertainty results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same input projection, multi-resolution time imaging, dual-axis decomposition, multi-scale and multi-resolution mixing, and prediction-head ensemble. No algorithm, architecture, or training-objective change is reported.

E1.justification: The same eight tasks and benchmark datasets remain represented. Although detailed imputation and few-shot appendix tables disappear, their ETT evaluations remain represented by the unchanged averages in Tables 4-5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Tables 4-5. Updated citations for iTransformer, TiDE, and Anomaly Transformer identify the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and sizes, forecasting horizons, imputation masking rates, the 10% few-shot training budget, zero-shot transfer pairs, metrics, and training settings are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is documented.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablations in Tables 7, 11, and 12, representation analyses, efficiency comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, and forecasting case studies. The removed tables contain benchmark breakdowns rather than additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three experimental runs and report standard deviations and statistical-test percentages, with the same classification uncertainty statement. Renaming 'Confidence Interval' to 'Confidence Level' does not establish a changed estimation procedure; revised numerical uncertainty outcomes are assessed under E6.

E6.justification: Tables 13-14 revise many standard deviations without changing means; Solar-Energy MSE changes from 0.203 ± 0.001 to 0.203 ± 0.027. Table 13 lowers reported confidence from 99% to 95% for Solar-Energy, Traffic, ETTh2, and ETTm2. Removing v2 Tables 19-20 also removes individual ETT imputation and few-shot results, while Tables 4-5 retain their averages. These changes affect uncertainty outcomes and result granularity; main benchmark means remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-11, the metric formulas in Appendix A, and the mathematical model description in Appendix B are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a general time series pattern machine combining multi-scale and multi-resolution processing, with claimed state-of-the-art performance across eight tasks.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of representation and ablation results, and Appendix K's limitations concerning data scale and model scaling remain unchanged. The revised uncertainty values receive no new interpretation or qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same software, A100 80GB hardware, optimizer and loss, batch size, hyperparameter ranges, and implementation guidance. The promised source-code and pretrained-model access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Reference edits update publication metadata and consolidate duplicate entries, including iTransformer and Non-stationary Transformers. Matching the underlying works establishes no substantive addition or removal of prior research, and Section 2's positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There is limited citation and bibliography cleanup, updated table cross-references, and a shortened Appendix H results overview. The section ordering, narrative, and substantive explanations remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 Tables 19-20 are removed, and the anomaly-detection and classification tables are renumbered from 21-22 to 19-20 and reflowed. Tables 13-15 receive corrected confidence-column headings. All 25 figures retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly reduces transparency by removing nonredundant ETT breakdowns from v2 Tables 19-20 while retaining broad superiority claims. For example, v2 exposes an ETTm2 imputation exception: TimeMixer++ MAE is 0.135 versus TimesNet's 0.124; v5 retains only the ETT average. Bibliographic cleanup and clearer confidence labels are useful, but do not compensate for losing these comparisons. The unexplained uncertainty revisions do not establish an additional quality improvement.
